set_aside.subject: audit log numbering across restored store histories
set_aside.text: “Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within each store's history” introduces “the log's numbering”, but no accepted text defines a log number, where it is stored, whether it is returned, or what invariant it has after restoration.
set_aside.question: What is the audit log's numbering guarantee, and after a restore does numbering continue from the backup's last entry, restart for a new history, or require a separately identified history/epoch?
options: Continue from the highest number present in the restored backup
Restart numbering and identify a new store history
Do not make numbering a product guarantee
set_aside.default_guess: Continue from the highest number present in the restored backup, with no separately exposed history identifier.

set_aside.subject: agent access after restoration
set_aside.text: R0-89 says “every change after it is lost” and Registry's guarantees hold only “within each store's history”, while R0-46 says that revoking a project makes “every later operation on it in that session” refused. Restoring a backup made before the revocation restores the grant and permits those later operations.
set_aside.question: Does a restore intentionally reinstate backed-up session grants, active projects and sessions, thereby narrowing R0-46, R0-47, R0-53 and R0-61, or must Registry preserve or reapply access removals across store histories?
options: Restore access state exactly as backed up and explicitly narrow the access guarantees
Preserve or reapply later revocations and removals
Invalidate all agent sessions and grants after a restored store starts
set_aside.default_guess: Restore the backed-up access state exactly, because Registry is told to start on the backup as on any store.

set_aside.subject: erasure and restriction after restoration
set_aside.text: R0-89 says that every change after the backup “is lost”, but the accepted actions say erased customer values “are gone”, erased audit entries “are gone”, an anonymised project is final, and restricted personal data reaches no service. A pre-change backup can restore all of those earlier values and states.
set_aside.question: May restoration resurrect customer personal data, projects, audit entries, or processing permissions that were erased, anonymised, deleted or restricted after the backup, or must those irreversible/privacy changes survive across store histories?
options: Literal snapshot rollback may resurrect them, explicitly narrowing the erasure, anonymisation and restriction guarantees
Registry must preserve or reapply irreversible and privacy-related changes after restore
Backups containing superseded personal or audit state must become ineligible for restore
set_aside.default_guess: Apply a literal snapshot rollback, including resurrection of the backed-up state, because R0-89 declares all later changes lost.

set_aside.subject: request replay after restoration
set_aside.text: R0-36 says “No retried request creates a duplicate”, and R0-88 says a retried publish returns the pointer it made; R0-89 permits restoring a backup that does not contain the original change or its replay record, while naming only R0-58 and R0-79 as narrowed.
set_aside.question: Are replay and idempotency guarantees reset at the restored backup boundary, so retrying a request accepted after that backup may create a new record or pointer, or must Registry retain enough replay knowledge outside the store to honor R0-36 and R0-88 across restoration?
options: Reset replay knowledge to the backup and explicitly narrow R0-36 and R0-88
Preserve replay records outside the restored store
Refuse previously issued request identifiers whose outcomes cannot be recovered
set_aside.default_guess: Reset replay knowledge to what the backup contains; a missing prior request is handled as new.
